note: Carousel no. 16 is unusually thin on arithmetic. Every printed numeral on its nine frames is quoted from a claim, so the only aggregates in the deck are three counting words in running copy. Each is declared here.

aggregates.computed_by: len(shares_from_c18) in out/2026-09-05/compute.py, which parses the import origins out of claim c18's own quote with a regular expression and asserts their names and their percentages before writing out/2026-09-05/computed.json
aggregates.why_not_from_claims: The five origins are five values inside ONE claim rather than five claims. Naming five claim ids for them would be the shape the count rule expects and a lie about where they came from, which is the reason the computed_by route exists.
aggregates.reads_on_the_frame: A federal survey lists where the United States gets the rare earth compounds and metals it imports. Five sources, and one of them is most of it.
aggregates.sources_here_means: import origins, which is what the survey line lists, and never a count of documents. The deck cites one document for it, c18.

aggregates.note: One claim per figure. c2 is Rice's $2.9 million and c3 is the University of Houston's $2.88 million, for the same award. The frame prints both and reconciles neither, so the count is of the figures published and not of a difference between them.

The term is the source's own word and not a span this deck measured. No start date and no end date are published anywhere in the record, so the deck can't compute a duration and does not try. c4 carries the same term as 'Over the three-year grant period'.
